details:
The Web Panel would be awesome to have and I REALLY want it back. However I don't know if this will ever happen. A dynamic image loader would be nice, sure - but bringing other kinds of content - like documents, books, news articles (think Virtual Week-ality) is still something you would have to re-upload your world for. I give you a compromise: Markdown Panels. 
Markdown is a pretty neat markup language that is used everywhere from github, reddit, discord, etc. It allows for bolding, italicizing, different headings, tables, code-blocks, in-line images, and more. 
This theoretical “Markdown Panel” could allow markdown (.md) documents to be dynamically loaded and displayed in-game, with URLs provided by either the world, or even by the user in a text box (similar to how video players use URLs). Markdown documents would be limited to linking to other .md documents, and possibly video/youtube URLs that could be redirected to a video player within the world. And unlike with HTML, this wouldn’t open up VRChat to custom code execution, one of the main concerns of bringing back the Web Panel. 
With the Markdown Panel, World creators could create library worlds with book readers, easily update changelogs, and display other information to visitors that can be updated externally without breaking open the Unity Editor. Users could share writing, articles, homework, and more with each other without risking custom JavaScript running on their machines. If necessary, this could be restricted by the “Custom URL” checkbox (with Github and VRChat’s CDN being whitelisted), or a more robust permission system if needed.  
TL;DR – VRChat needs a better way to get information/content into worlds without re-uploading them. External markdown documents seem like a pretty cool way to do this should a new Web Panel be impossible, with more uses than I could think of right now.
title: Markdown Panel
